We propose reinstating the BA for all eligible students in order to serve the shifting demographic of our student body as well as refine our BFA program to introduce more rigorous standards appropriate to a pre-professional training program.
The Rhode Island Promise Act has increased the number of transfer students considerably, making it highly difficult for those students to complete a BFA in 4 years.
Additionally, the number of double majors/minors has increased making it equally difficult for those students to complete the very narrow BFA curriculum without impact to their other majors (particularly those, such as Nursing, who also have to meet clinical requirements that tend to conflict with our required courses).
A BA offers more flexibility for order of courses, thus making it more feasible for our transfer students and those completing more than one major.
URI Theatre completed an External Review in Spring of 2024.
Among their recommendations was to standardize evaluation tools across our curriculum and instate more rigorous standards for degree completion, including capstone performances and projects.

Many BFA programs also involve standards that, if not met, result in dismissal from the program.
It has never been the policy of URI theatre to dismiss students from our program except in very rare cases of academic failure.
Introducing this type of standardization is possible if we have the option to invite students to our BA program in the event that the BFA curriculum is not a good fit.
Bifurcating our program in this way allows URI Theatre to serve the widest number of students while also introducing more clear standards for our BFA students.
The reinstatement of the BA does not require any new courses or staffing.
Students in the BA program will be taking courses already offered in our existing curriculum but have more choice in terms of when and what they take.

Rationale for Proposed Changes perThe23Theatre BA is currently suspended and only open to those students who are pursuing a degree in Elementary Education.
We propose reinstating the BA for all eligible students in order to serve the shifting demographic of our student body as well as refine our BFA program to introduce more rigorous standards appropriate to a pre-24professional training program.
The Rhode Island Promise Act has increased the number of transfer students considerably, making it highly difficult for those students to complete a BFA in 4 years.
Additionally, the number of double majors/minors has increased making it equally difficult for those students to complete the very narrow BFA curriculum without impact to their other majors (particularly those, such as Nursing, who also have to meet clinical requirements that tend to conflict with our required courses).
A BA offers more flexibility for order of courses, thus making it more feasible for our transfer students and those completing more than one major.
URI Theatre completed an External Review in Spring of 2024.

Among their recommendations was to standardize evaluation tools across our curriculum and instate more rigorous standards for degree completion, including capstone performances and projects.
M any BFA programs also involve standards that, if not met, result in dismissal from the program.
It has never been the policy of URI theatre to dismiss students from our program except in very rare cases of academic failure.
Introducing this type of standardization is possible if we have the option to invite students to our BA program in the event that the BFA curriculum is not a good fit.
Bifurcating our program in this way allows URI Theatre to serve the widest number of students while also introducing more clear standards for our BFA students.
The reinstatement of the BA does not require any new courses or staffing.
Students in the BA program will be taking courses already offered in our existing curriculum but have more choice in terms of when and what they take.

Because our program has undergone some changes to course codes since the suspension of the BA, we include here the courses we propose for completion of the BA in Theatre: Core Courses (total of 33 credits): THE111 (Introduction to Acting), THE161 (Introduction to Stagecraft), THE181 (Script Analysis), THE221 (Introduction to Stage M anagement), THE250 (Costume Laboratory), THE251 (Introduction to Design), THE307 or THE338G (Creative Dramatics or Ethics in Theatre), THE321 (Orientation to Directing), THE381 (Theatre History to 1642), THE382 (Theatre History: Neoclassical through 19th century), and either THE351, 352, 383, 384 OR 481 (these are advanced design or special topics courses) for a total of 33 required credits.
Optional electives within the major include THE112, THE200, THE300, THE400.
For many students, this would include participating in our production season for which they receive course credit (THE200/300/400).
Students must complete a minimum of 30 credits at the 300-20level or above (these may include 300-level courses offered inside the major or courses offered outside the program).

The B.S. program in interdisciplinary neuroscience will provide students with foundational knowledge of the nervous system including a broad array of areas such as development of the nervous system, brain structure and function, cellular and molecular biology, neuropharmacology, neuroethics, research methods, as well as knowledge of neurodegenerative disease and psychological/psychiatric disorders.
The undergraduate program offers three major options (tracks): a B.S. degree with a major in Clinical Neuroscience from the College of Health Sciences, a B.S. degree with a major in M olecular Neuroscience from the College of Environment and Life Sciences, and a B.S. degree with a major in M edicinal Neuroscience from the College of Pharmacy.
The option for different neuroscience majors is unique and makes this URI major truly distinct with regard to undergraduate education.
Please note: students may only earn a Neuroscience degree in one track due to the overlapping of preparation and core courses needed for the major.
Careers Students who graduate with this B.S. have an ever-growing choice of career options.

These include graduate school in neuroscience, medical school, graduate programs in allied health professions; research positions in academic, government, biotech or pharmaceutical laboratories; and a variety of professional opportunities in science education, science writing, data science, and health care.
Requirements The B.S. program requires a minimum of 120 credits for graduation: 40-43 preparation, 35-38 core, 40 general education (some of these credits/courses will overlap with your preparation credits/courses), and 18 in your chosen major/track (clinical, molecular, or medicinal).
To transfer out of University College for Academic Success and enter your selected degree granting college, you must complete a minimum of 56 credits of the following courses with a 2.0 GPA average: BIO 101/103, BIO 102/104, BIO 220/221, BIO 222/223, CHM 101/102, CHM 112/114, CHM 124 or 227, PHY 111/185, M TH 103/131, PSY 113, COM 100, WRT 104 or 106, URI 101, NEU 101, NEU 110, NEU 210, NEU 262, and NEU 230.

This major prepares undergraduates for a career as a Registered Dietitian/Nutritionist (RDN).
The M .S. in Nutrition includes an Accelerated Bachelors to M asters of Science (ABM ) option for students enrolled in the B.S. degree, described below.
This Dietetics degree is required for all students planning to become RDNs.
URI's Dietetics program is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Education in Nutrition and Dietetics (ACEND), 120 South Riverside Plaza, Suite 2190, Chicago, IL 60606. 800.877.1600, ext. 5400; https://www.eatrightpro.org/acend/.
Please see the department website for complete program information (https://web.uri.edu/nutrition/).

The dietetics major requires 27 credits in sciences (four in general chemistry [CHM 103/105], four in organic chemistry [CHM 124/126], three in biochemistry [CM B 210], twelve in biology [BIO 110/103; 220/221; 222/223], and four in microbiology [CM B 201/202]), 4 credits in general nutrition (NUT 207/210), 4 credits in introductory professional courses (NUT 110 and 212G); and 4138 credits in the concentration including the following courses: NUT 336, 337, 375, 376, 394396, 395, 410, 440, 441, 443, 444, 445, and 458 [capstone].
Additionally, M GT 341 is required and COM 100, M TH 103, PSY 113, SOC 100, STA 220, and WRT 104 are required and may be used to fulfill general education requirements.
There are 17 credits of free electives.
Students are encouraged to use free electives to study disciplines related to the field.
Students must maintain a 3.00 average in all required courses (NUT courses, science courses, and the remaining degree courses), with no less than a C in any one class, in order to graduate.
A total of 120 credits is required for graduation.

Students will be admitted to the dietetics degree program after completing a minimum of 30 credits, including CHM 103/105; CHM 124; BIO 220/221; WRT 104; COM 100; NUT 207 and 210; BIO 110/103; and M TH 103.
Students must maintain a 3.00 average in all required courses (NUT courses, science courses, and the remaining degree courses) completed when being evaluated for admission, with no less than a C in any one class, in order to graduate.
Students may repeat NUT courses once.
After completing their B.S. requirements, students can qualify for the professional title of Registered Dietitian/Nutritionist by completing supervised practice requirements and graduate degree, and passing a national credentialing exam.
